parsed.explanation: A fresh (Dec 2024) penal code criminalises same-sex conduct by birth-assigned sex with 2–5 years' imprisonment, plus an open-ended 'promotion' offence. Since it took effect, arbitrary arrests and physical abuse based on appearance or gender expression alone have risen — documented state-directed targeting of the gender-nonconforming, not a dormant statute. A trans visitor in any close relationship or with gender-nonconforming presentation falls inside its terms by definition. No anti-discrimination protection, no complaint mechanism, a junta whose justice minister framed homosexuality as unnatural, and near-total documented societal hostility (98% rejection). Severity (imprisonment, custodial abuse) and frequency (post-code arrest surge) are both documented; only the scale of the surge is unquantified. No entry/document rules specific to trans travellers are documented, but discovery converts directly into criminal exposure. This sits between the 0.15 sweep-pattern anchors and the 0.05 lethal-outcome anchors, nearer the former.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry rule, visa provision, screening or identity-document requirement specific to transgender travellers is documented; ordinary passport checks are the exposure baseline.
entry_documents.interaction: Once documents or presentation trigger any police contact, the encounter enters the criminal-code regime; no documented checkpoint-specific practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented significant rise since 13 Dec 2024 in arbitrary arrests and detentions of people targeted on appearance or gender expression alone; 'promotion' offence is undefined and expansively applicable; penalties 2–5 years plus fine.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented; no domestic complaint mechanism exists.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Junta-controlled justice system; courts unlikely to offer relief; arrest escalates directly into imprisonment exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison placement, segregation or custody conditions for trans detainees are not documented; detention abuse (physical abuse of gender-nonconforming arrestees) is documented qualitatively.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Custody follows any enforcement action nationwide with no subnational variation documented.

care_services.interaction: No data on medication continuity or emergency-care treatment of trans visitors; thin dossier resolves toward the hostile structural climate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing is explicit: justice minister calls homosexuality unnatural, code justified as defending 'traditional and moral values'; Article 225 public-indecency enforcement against gender-nonconforming expression predates and predicts the new code's application.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law and enforcement align against trans people; rule of law operates as liability, not recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for trans minors or travelling guardians specifically; the 'promotion' offence could sweep in anyone associated with a gender-nonconforming adult, but no child-specific rule is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Arrest of the accompanying adult under the code would leave a minor exposed indirectly; speculative, not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented post-code increase in physical abuse based on appearance or gender expression alone; significant societal stigma and 98% rejection of homosexuality; violence context includes armed groups (general, secondary).
street_violence_police_response.protection: No anti-discrimination law, no protection body, no documented police protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are perpetrators, not protectors; reporting increases exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No domestic remedy of any kind documented; association ban prevents community support infrastructure; scale of arrest surge unquantified; trans-specific societal attitudes undocumented (data addresses homosexuality/MSM).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-data jurisdiction resolves toward the risk implied by criminalisation, junta rule, active prior enforcement and absence of any relief.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar structural pattern: enforcement actively directed at presentation/gender expression, coerced-custody abuse, no functioning recourse, morality-law framing. This dossier lacks documented decoy sweeps and capital-clause ambiguity but documents a fresh nationwide code plus a post-code arrest and abuse surge — comparable tier, slight edge above 0.15-C on severity of organised state targeting.

0.25-D features selective morality enforcement with courts occasionally annulling cases. Here courts are junta-controlled, no appellate relief is documented, and arrests have risen since the code took effect — enforcement is documented, not selective extortion; this jurisdiction rates clearly below 0.25-D.

0.05-D documents a complete arrest-to-execution chain. This dossier's maximum documented penalty is 2–5 years with no capital provision for gender-related conduct and no lethal outcome documented; the custodial-abuse record is qualitative. Materially less severe than the 0.05 tier, though the junta climate keeps uncertainty weighted toward risk.

0.35-B ends at hours-long detention and fines. This jurisdiction carries multi-year imprisonment, documented physical abuse of gender-nonconforming arrestees, and zero complaint mechanisms — a full severity tier below 0.35-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a single nationwide junta-enforced criminal code: same-sex conduct defined by birth-assigned sex, an undefined 'promotion' offence, no recognised affirmed gender, no anti-discrimination protection, and a pre-existing Article 225 enforcement record against gender-nonconforming expression that the post-code surge of arrests and physical abuse confirms continues. Discovery — through any relationship, police contact, or visible presentation — flows directly into arbitrary arrest and custodial abuse with no remedy at any stage. The severity (2–5 years' imprisonment, physical abuse) is short of the lethal tier, and no capital pathway is documented; the arrest-surge magnitude is unquantified but the targeting of appearance alone is documented. Interactions compound: state threat-framing, a hostile society (98% rejection), banned associations, and a justice system the junta controls all close off recourse. The rating sits just above the 0.05 lethal-outcome anchors and at the bottom of the enforcement-based band, ~0.14.
